photo.caption: Remains of the Imperial palace of Mediolanum (Milan). The imperial palace (built in large part by Maximian, colleague of Diocletian) was a large complex with several buildings, gardens, and courtyards, used for the Emperor's private and public activities, and for his court, family, and imperial bureaucracy.
photo.description: Ruins of the Ancient Roman imperial palace in via Brisa in Milan, Italy. Milan become, in the 4th century AD, the capital of the Western portion of the Roman Empire. In this view a circular corridor with some rooms around, the circle on the centre was probably surrounded by columns. Shot by Lorenzo Fratti, 2007.
